title: Time Expressions — Classify by Tense
hint: If the time expression points to a finished moment in the past, it goes with past simple. If it links the past to now, it goes with present perfect.
prompt: Drag each time expression into the tense it most often goes with.

feedback.correct: Nicely classified. Past simple is for finished past moments tied to a specific time; present perfect connects an unfinished or recently-finished period to now. Notice how 'in May 2019' (a specific past moment) goes with past simple while 'since 2020' (a period that includes now) goes with present perfect.
feedback.incorrect: Re-check the time expressions one by one. The diagnostic is whether the expression locates an action at a finished past moment (past simple) or links a past action to now (present perfect). 'Never' and 'always-up-to-now' phrasings ('all my life') are present perfect; specific past dates ('a year ago', 'yesterday', 'in May 2019') are past simple.
